question.text:
Given the following expression grammar:

$$
\begin{gathered}
E \rightarrow E+T|T * E| T \\
T \rightarrow T / F \mid F \\
F \rightarrow \mathrm{id}
\end{gathered}
$$


Which of the following is/are true?

  1. $*$ has higher precedence than $+$
     
  2. $/$ has higher precedence than $*$
     
  3. $+$ is left-associative
     
  4. $*$ is right-associative
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following grammar with semantic actions inside braces:

  • $S \rightarrow a A \quad$ {print "1"}
     
  • $S \rightarrow b \quad$ {print " 2 " }
     
  • $A \rightarrow S b \quad$ {print " 3 " }

If we perform a leftmost derivation for the string $a a b b b$ and execute the actions as soon as the leftmost nonterminal in the sentential form is replaced, what is the printed output?
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
A shift-reduce parser carries out the actions specified within braces immediately after reducing with the corresponding rule of the grammar:

  • $A \rightarrow a B \quad$ {print "1"}
     
  • $A \rightarrow b \quad$    {print "2"}
     
  • $B \rightarrow A c$     {print "3"}

What is the translation of $a a b c c$ using the syntax-directed translation scheme described by the above rules?

  1. $23131$
     
  2. $21323$
     
  3. $21321$
     
  4. $12312$
question.subject: Compiler Design
